filings.title: April 2026 rebase, part 3
filings.summary: Rounding or measuring a span in months from the 29th, 30th or 31st can answer against the wrong pair of dates, because the polyfill never rechecks that the window it searched contains the date it is aiming for. The maintainer had already written this fix, so rather than file a duplicate we added what it was missing: a way to reproduce the bug, a scan of Chromium 153 against the published release, and before-and-after measurements of the fix applied on main.

filings.title: Polyfill: Validate result in UTC fast path in GetPossibleEpochNanoseconds
filings.summary: Near the end of the supported range, a calculation in the UTC time zone quietly returns a wrong value where it should report an error. The shortcut the code takes for UTC skips the range check that every other time zone goes through.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer is applying the upstream changes in order and asked to keep it that way, so this one arrives in its turn rather than ahead of it.

filings.title: Polyfill: Update Meiji era start date
filings.summary: The Japanese calendar puts dates from 1868 to the end of 1872 in the Meiji era, where the standard asks for the Gregorian-equivalent era. The era and era-year are wrong for those five years.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer is applying the upstream changes in order and asked to keep it that way, so this one arrives in its turn rather than ahead of it.

filings.title: Polyfill: Fix extreme PlainYearMonth crash in non-ISO calendars
filings.summary: Converting a Hebrew, Islamic, Coptic-family or Indian calendar date near either end of the supported range fails with an Invalid ISO date error, even though the date asked for is a real one.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer is applying the upstream changes in order and asked to keep it that way, so this one arrives in its turn rather than ahead of it.

filings.title: Don't format dates past the range limit when counting months in until()
filings.summary: Counting months between two dates in a non-ISO calendar fails when the later date falls in the first or last month of the supported range. The month-by-month loop builds a date beyond the range that it never actually needs.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer will apply the fix to the Temporal standard first, and it reaches the polyfill from there.

filings.title: Search the last partial window when looking for the next time zone transition
filings.summary: Looking for the next time zone transition in roughly the last two months of the supported range can report that there is none, when there is one. startOfDay, hoursInDay and toZonedDateTime then fail instead of returning an answer.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer will apply the fix to the Temporal standard first, and it reaches the polyfill from there.

filings.title: Start the time zone transition search before the first transition in 1844
filings.summary: Time zone lookups before 1847 miss a real transition on 31 December 1844 in five zones: Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones. The search starts at 1847, which used to be the earliest transition anyone had recorded and no longer is.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer will apply the fix to the Temporal standard first, and it reaches the polyfill from there.

filings.title: Release request: main has fixes that 0.5.1 doesn't (ZonedDateTime near the Instant limits, #341, #347)
filings.summary: Anyone using the published 0.5.1 release still meets several bugs that were fixed 76 commits ago on the project's main branch, among them failures for valid zoned dates near both ends of the range and two calendar-conversion bugs. No release has been published to bring those fixes to them.

filings.title: Removing time zone canonicalization in `Intl.DateTimeFormat` will change behavior of Temporal polyfills
filings.summary: When `Intl.DateTimeFormat` stops canonicalizing time zone ids, the polyfills compare zones wrongly. Our comment shows that in WebKit, which already works that way, `UTC` and `Etc/UTC` compare unequal and `until` throws, and that the `UTC` case can be fixed without time zone data.

filings.title: Polyfill: non-ISO until() by months gives wrong results since #3245, and throws near the range limits
filings.summary: Counting months between two dates in a non-ISO calendar has given a wrong answer since a recent change, at ordinary dates as well as unusual ones. Adding the answer back to the first date no longer lands on the second, and near the ends of the range the count fails outright.

filings.title: Polyfill: GetNamedTimeZoneNextTransition misses a transition in the last search window before the max Instant
filings.summary: Looking for the next time zone transition in the last stretch before the end of the supported range can report that there is none, when there is one. Code that relies on the answer then fails instead of getting one.

filings.title: Polyfill: calendarToIsoDate overshoot assertion from #3292 is reachable in coptic/ethiopic/ethioaa month 13
filings.summary: Building a Coptic, Ethiopic or Ethioaa date in the thirteenth month can fail an internal check instead of returning the date. The search moves eight days at a time, on the assumption that it can never step over a whole month, but that month is only five or six days long.
filings.gmtNote: GMT computes coptic and ethiopic dates through ethioaa and finds a date from its calendar fields by bisection, so this search-step bug can't affect it. A canary check (D10) watches for it in every polyfill release.

filings.title: Polyfill: time zone transitions before 1847 are not found (Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones on 1844-12-31)
filings.summary: Time zone lookups before 1847 miss a real transition on 31 December 1844 in five zones: Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones. The search assumes no zone has a transition before 1847, which the time zone database contradicts.

filings.title: ZonedDateTime.from rejects ZonedDateTime.prototype.toString's output when the local date is -271821-04-19
filings.summary: A zoned date and time in the first hours of the supported range, in a time zone west of Greenwich, prints as a string that reading it back then refuses. The spec checks the local date against the date range before it matches the offset, so the string fails although the moment it names is in range. The issue asks whether that check is meant.
filings.gmtNote: GMT follows the spec text here, as Chromium, Node and the polyfill do, so there is no workaround to retire. Its zoned readers (isValidZonedDateTime, toOffsetInstant, classifyStoredZoned and the rest) refuse a string whose local date is -271821-04-19. If the spec drops the check, they drop it too.
filings.outcome: Closed as answered: the check is intended. The Temporal champions had already said so on #3014, and it can go once tc39/ecma262#3464 lands.

filings.title: Polyfill: getTimeZoneTransition throws a bisection assertion for Africa/El_Aaiun in 1976
filings.summary: Looking for the next or previous time zone transition in Africa/El_Aaiun in spring 1976 can throw an internal assertion instead of answering. Two transitions there are just under 17 days apart, and the search window for that zone is 17 days, so one window can hold both. The issue proposes a 16-day window.

filings.title: Polyfill: Temporal.Now reads a millisecond before Date.now() after a pre-1970 clock reading
filings.summary: After the clock reads a date before 1970, the next Temporal.Now reading can land a millisecond before Date.now(), so a 2027 clock can read as the last millisecond of 2026. The polyfill carries the previous reading's milliseconds modulo a million as a sub-millisecond part, and the remainder keeps its minus sign. In js-temporal's polyfill, fake timers in tests hit this whenever they set a pre-1970 date. The issue proposes a floor modulo.

filings.title: Failed Assert in NudgeToCalendarUnit when a duration ends in the later pass of a repeated hour
filings.summary: Measuring a length in days or weeks across a repeated or skipped hour can fail an internal check in the spec, when the length ends just past the edge of a day or week. The spec places that edge with the "compatible" rule, which can put it on the wrong side of the end, and its second try cannot move a day or week edge. Chromium throws and the polyfill returns a number the spec does not give, so GMT returns its sentinel for these lengths. The issue asks which answer is meant.

filings.title: Polyfill: ZonedDateTime.from reads a `Z` string by wall clock when `offset` is `ignore`
filings.summary: Reading a string that ends in `Z` with `offset: "ignore"` should keep the exact time the string names. The polyfill reads the string's wall-clock time in the target zone instead, so the result is off by that zone's offset.

filings.title: Polyfill: Islamic dates before 1 AH throw `Era before-hijra was not matched by any era` in WebKit
filings.summary: In WebKit, the polyfill throws for Islamic dates before 1 AH, because WebKit's formatter prints those years in a `Before Hijra` era the polyfill does not recognise. V8 prints those dates as `AH` with a negative year, so the polyfill works there.

filings.title: Polyfill: `toLocaleString` takes Temporal formats from `resolvedOptions()`, so `month: 'long'` prints a numeric month in zh and ja
filings.summary: `toLocaleString` builds its Temporal formats from `resolvedOptions()` rather than from the caller's options, so in Chinese and Japanese `month: "long"` or `"short"` prints a numeric month. V8 has the same problem (Chromium 553245554).
filings.gmtNote: GMT never calls `toLocaleString`: its formatters pass the caller's own options to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, so the month width the caller asks for is kept.

filings.title: Polyfill: `multiple instants found` is thrown for a wall-clock time that has no instant
filings.summary: With `disambiguation: "reject"`, a wall-clock time in a gap throws `multiple instants found`, though a time in a gap has no instant at all. The same text is right for a repeated time, so the gap case needs its own message.
filings.gmtNote: GMT never shows this message: under `"reject"`, `resolveLocal` returns `""` for a skipped or repeated time instead of throwing.

filings.title: `PlainDate.from` accepts malformed RFC 9557 annotations
filings.summary: Date parsing accepts strings RFC 9557 rejects: an empty annotation such as `2024-10-03[]`, a calendar annotation before the time zone, or an annotation value containing `;` or `=`.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.7.

filings.title: `ZonedDateTime.from` rejects the two instants at the ends of the `Instant` range
filings.summary: `ZonedDateTime.from` rejects the two exact instants at the ends of Temporal's range, such as `-271821-04-20T00:00:00Z[Asia/Tokyo]`, which the standard accepts.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.7.

filings.title: Wrong UTC offset all through the period between two close offset changes (follow-up to #73)
filings.summary: When a zone's offset changes twice within a few weeks, the polyfill skips the period between the changes and reads the wrong offset all through it, as in `Africa/Casablanca` during Ramadan in 2018. A daily check of every zone found it in 11 zones.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.7.

filings.title: `getTimeZoneTransition("previous")` skips every transition more than three years after today
filings.summary: Searching back for a zone's last transition never returns one later than about three years from today. From any later date it returns an older transition, so the answer depends on the day the code runs.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.8.

filings.title: Time zone transitions before 1847 are not found (`Asia/Manila` and four Pacific zones on 1844-12-31)
filings.summary: Transitions before 1847 are not found, so `Asia/Manila` and four Pacific zones miss their offset change on 31 December 1844.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.8.

filings.title: Persian calendar: 78 years from 1502 to 2987 AP get the wrong leap year
filings.summary: The Persian calendar uses the plain 33-year leap rule, where ICU4X corrects 78 years from 1502 to 2987 AP. In the year after each one, every date reads one day early.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets these Persian years right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: Chinese and Dangi: dates read from Intl differ from native Temporal (Chinese New Year 2027)
filings.summary: Chinese and Dangi dates are read from `Intl`, which on Node 26 (ICU 78.3) disagrees with native Temporal. Chinese New Year 2027 falls on 7 February instead of 6 February.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, whose 0.5.1 release throws on Chinese and Dangi dates under ICU 78 instead (js-temporal/temporal-polyfill#360, fixed on its `main` and not yet released). GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: Apply the ICU4X leap-year corrections to the Persian calendar
filings.summary: The Persian calendar skips the corrections ICU4X makes to 78 leap years from 1502 to 2987 AP, so the first day of the year after each one reads as an extra 30th day of month 12, every other day of that year one day early, and the leap-year answers are wrong for both years. This applies the same corrections as ICU4X.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets these Persian years right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: Compute the Chinese and Dangi calendars like ICU4X instead of reading Intl
filings.summary: Computes Chinese and Dangi dates the way ICU4X, and so native Temporal, does, from its year tables for 1900 to 2102 and its mean-motion rule outside them, instead of reading them from the host's `Intl`. Dates no longer change with the host's ICU version, and dates near the end of Temporal's range no longer throw. It also fixes `until` and `since` from a leap month the end year lacks.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, whose 0.5.1 release throws on Chinese and Dangi dates under ICU 78 instead (js-temporal/temporal-polyfill#360, fixed on its `main` and not yet released). GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: Round Duration#total results once
filings.summary: `Duration#total` in weeks, months or years can come out one unit in the last place away from the correctly rounded value, because the polyfill rounds twice where the spec asks for one division. Someone else had already sent the fix, so we added two reproducing cases and showed that the difference breaks the project's own parity tests on Node 26.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: FormatDateTimePattern: "value ≤ 0, set value to 1 − value" is wrong for calendars with a single era
filings.summary: ECMA-402 turns a year of 0 or below into 1 minus the year for every calendar, but only a calendar with an inverse era needs that. The indian and persian calendars have one signed era, so `-79 Śaka` and `-622 AP` are right, and native Temporal already gives those years.
filings.gmtNote: GMT prints the year the engine prints and keeps no year rule of its own, so this changes nothing in GMT.

filings.title: Intl.DateTimeFormat formatToParts aborts the process (unreachable code) when the locale pattern has Y: please cherry-pick V8 0426b0d1045d into v22.x, v24.x and v26.x
filings.summary: Node stops the whole process when `formatToParts` or `formatRangeToParts` formats a date with a pattern that holds the week-of-year year, which some languages' patterns do. It asks Node 22, 24 and 26 to take the V8 fix that Chromium 158 already has.

filings.title: Temporal on v26.x: until() and round() add one smallestUnit to a whole number of years, months or weeks (temporal_rs 0.2.3)
filings.summary: Node 26 adds one `smallestUnit` when it rounds a whole number of years, months or weeks. It asks Node 26 to move to `temporal_rs` 0.2.4 or later, or to take the one fix (boa-dev/temporal#723) on its own.
filings.gmtNote: GMT makes no change: it already follows the spec text, and `@js-temporal/polyfill` 0.5.1 is right.

filings.title: v26.x: Intl.DateTimeFormat specification bugs when formatting Temporal objects
filings.summary: Asks Node 26 to take two V8 fixes for Temporal `toLocaleString`: an `era` option on its own drops the year and month, and a Chinese or Japanese full date loses its long month name.
filings.gmtNote: GMT is not affected: it never calls `toLocaleString`, and its formatters pass the caller's own options to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

filings.title: Incorrect use of week-based year (Y) in gl and kek date patterns
filings.summary: Some languages' date patterns print the week-of-year year where the calendar year belongs. The ticket names gl and kek, and our comment adds the other patterns on `main`, the gd and te repros and the Node crash.

filings.title: Interval formats that drop, repeat or misplace a field (yo, rw, sw, brx, dz, en_JP, kgp, yrl, ku, qu, rm, sv, th, wae, ta)
filings.summary: Interval patterns in 15 languages drop, repeat or misplace a field when a range is formatted: yo, rw, sw, brx, dz, en-JP, kgp, yrl, ku, qu, rm, sv, th, wae and ta. It includes the rw `yMMMd` pattern that CLDR 49 adds and the ta `hmv` pattern.

filings.title: Interval formats that write a field in a different form from the single date, or run two fields together (fur, gsw, ksh, mn, brx, zh iso8601, root chinese)
filings.summary: Interval patterns in fur, gsw, ksh and mn write the month in a different form from the single date. They also run two fields together in brx and in zh with the iso8601 calendar, and the root locale drops the chinese related year.

filings.title: PersianCalendar::isLeapYear returns true for every year before 0 since ICU4C 75
filings.summary: ICU4C 75 and later counts every Persian year before year 0 as a leap year, because a C++ `%` rounds toward zero. WebKit on macOS shows it.
filings.gmtNote: Only GMT running on macOS WebKit's own `Temporal` sees it, where `addDate` and `subtractDate` return `""` for the dates it breaks. GMT on the polyfill is right.

filings.title: Japanese calendar: use the Gregorian era for 1868-10-23 to 1872-12-31 (Meiji 1–5)
filings.summary: The japanese calendar prints a date before 1873 in a Japanese era, where the standard asks for the Gregorian era up to the end of 1872. ICU 79 fixes most of it but still prints Meiji 1 to 5 for 1868-10-23 to 1872-12-31.

filings.title: ja@calendar=japanese: a two-digit year (yy) prints one digit when the pattern contains 年
filings.summary: A `ja` date in the japanese calendar with `year: "2-digit"` prints `令和6年` where the standard asks for `令和06年`, because ICU's Japanese year numbering ignores the minimum digit count.

filings.title: DateTimePatternGenerator turns a yy skeleton into a padded rr related year (Chinese, Dangi)
filings.summary: Under `year: "2-digit"` the chinese and dangi calendars print the related year padded to two digits, where ECMA-402 prints it at full width.

filings.title: DateIntervalFormat: a flexible day period (B) is printed once for two periods, and a chinese or dangi skeleton with U falls back to a pattern that loses fields
filings.summary: ICU prints the flexible day period B once for two different periods, and the chinese and dangi U skeletons fall back to patterns that lose fields.

filings.title: DateIntervalFormat: when only the era differs, the range uses the y entry and prints one era, so one date loses its era
filings.summary: When two dates differ only in their era, ICU takes the `y` interval pattern, which prints the era once, so one date loses its era: `scn` in the gregorian calendar, and ca, chr, fi, hr, it and ko in the ethiopic, japanese and roc calendars.

filings.title: DateIntervalFormat: an hour cycle set by the caller is not applied when the interval pattern comes from CLDR with a different hour letter (ja hm)
filings.summary: A `ja` range with `hourCycle: "h12"` keeps the `K` hour of the CLDR interval pattern and prints `0時` where the single date prints 12.

filings.title: DateIntervalFormat: the long flexible day period width is not applied to B, so a range prints AM or PM where the single date prints the wide period
filings.summary: Under `dayPeriod: "long"` a range keeps the stored `B` width, so in 22 locales such as bgc, to, sd and gaa it prints AM or PM where the single date prints the wide period.

filings.title: IslamicCalendar: civilLeapYear makes every year before 1 AH a leap year
filings.summary: ICU's tabular Islamic calendar counts every year before 1 AH as a leap year, because its leap-year test uses a remainder that is negative for negative years. ICU4C and ICU4J share the line.
filings.gmtNote: GMT has no workaround for this: it shows only through engines that use this ICU code for Temporal, which today is WebKit (WebKit 331725).

filings.title: IndianCalendar::handleComputeMonthStart truncates a negative Julian day, so months before Julian Day 0 start one day late
filings.summary: ICU starts every Indian-calendar month before Julian Day 0 one day late, because it truncates a negative day number instead of rounding it down. ICU4C and ICU4J share the bug.
filings.gmtNote: GMT has no workaround for this: it shows only through engines that use this ICU code for Temporal, which today is WebKit (WebKit 331726).

filings.title: Temporal’s Intl stringification for CJK is incorrect
filings.summary: V8 prints a numeric month in Chinese and Japanese for Temporal `toLocaleString` with `month: "long"`. A V8 fix covers the full date; our comment shows the cases it misses, where the Temporal type drops a field such as the day.
filings.gmtNote: GMT never calls `toLocaleString`: its formatters pass the caller's own options to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, so the month width the caller asks for is kept.

filings.title: Intl.DateTimeFormat keeps the "islamic" and "islamic-rgsa" calendars instead of the Intl era and monthCode fallbacks
filings.summary: V8 keeps `islamic` and `islamic-rgsa` as the resolved calendar. ECMA-402 turns `islamic` into `islamic-tbla` and no longer has `islamic-rgsa`, and WebKit 26.6 does both.

filings.title: Temporal and Intl reject the time zone ids CST6CDT, EST5EDT, MST7MDT and PST8PDT
filings.summary: WebKit 26.6 rejects the time zone ids `CST6CDT`, `EST5EDT`, `MST7MDT` and `PST8PDT` in `Intl` and `Temporal`, although the time zone database defines all four as zones. Chromium, Firefox and Node accept them.
filings.gmtNote: GMT has no workaround for this: it asks the engine about a time zone id, so these four read as invalid input on WebKit until the bug is fixed.

filings.title: [JSC][Intl] Islamic era override ignores the formatter time zone, so 1 Muharram 1 AH formats as year 0 of Before Hijra
filings.summary: WebKit switches Islamic dates from `Before Hijra` to `AH` at a fixed instant instead of at local midnight, so the first hours of 1 AH print as year 0 in UTC and in every zone east of −07:52:58.

filings.title: [JSC][Temporal] islamic-civil, islamic-tbla and islamic-umalqura report every negative year as a leap year, so add({ years: 1 }) from M12 day 30 lands 13 months on
filings.summary: WebKit's Temporal treats every Islamic year before 1 AH as a leap year, so adding a year to the 30th of Dhu al-Hijjah lands 13 months on. The cause is in ICU, filed as ICU-23626.
filings.gmtNote: GMT has no workaround for this: it shows only when GMT runs on WebKit's own Temporal, where the native-suite rows that hit it are tagged with this report until WebKit is fixed.

filings.title: [JSC][Temporal] indian calendar add() and until() throw RangeError when the result is the last day of a month starting on or before ISO -004713-11-24
filings.summary: WebKit's Temporal throws when adding years or months lands on the last day of an Indian month that starts before Julian Day 0. The cause is in ICU, filed as ICU-23627.
filings.gmtNote: GMT has no workaround for this: it shows only when GMT runs on WebKit's own Temporal, where the native-suite rows that hit it are tagged with this report until WebKit is fixed.

filings.title: Intl.DateTimeFormat formatRange prints AM/PM instead of the dayPeriod when timeZoneName is set
filings.summary: Firefox's `formatRange` prints AM/PM instead of the flexible day period when `timeZoneName` is set. A single `format` in Firefox, and `formatRange` in every other engine, print the day period.

listings.summary: Suggests @northguild/gmt for the Date section, as an issue because pull requests there are limited to collaborators.
listings.title: Add GMT to Date

listings.summary: Adds a "Built on" column and an @northguild/gmt row to the Brief Comparison table, an @northguild/gmt column to Feature Parity, and an @northguild/gmt example to each how-to section.
listings.title: Add a Built on column and @northguild/gmt to the comparison
